name: Victoria Hurley
strapLine3: for building polished, accessible web applications.
intro1: My journey into software began with a fascination for how complex systems are built from the ground up. Before I was architecting digital interfaces, I was a luthier with a First Class Honours degree in Music Technology with a focus on guitar making. Whether carving a fretboard or refactoring a reactive Angular component, my approach remains the same: a deep respect for precision, durability, and the user’s experience with the final 'instrument'.
intro2: For over four years, I've been embedded on the British Airways account, moving across five product teams, from an AWS IoT proof of concept to the Seat Map and Disruptions flows. Along the way, I've become the engineer teams rely on for accessibility and for getting new developers up to speed, with hands-on backend work in NestJS, AWS and Terraform on the Seat Map and Ready to Travel projects. Outside work, I'm building full-stack applications of my own, including an AI-powered gardening platform, as I move towards full-stack roles.

experiences.title: Software engineer
description: Embedded consultant on the British Airways account for over four years, working across five product teams on customer-facing flows.

Seat Map (Angular / NestJS): joined as the first developer after the tech lead and helped interview the team's QA engineer. As the team's legacy expert, handled all release activity for the legacy Seat Map and onboarded engineers onto the codebase.
Sole engineer on the Seat Map accessibility project, working independently from audit reports to achieve WCAG compliance across the legacy pages.
Led the redesign of the legacy seat itinerary page, planning the flow of work across a three-engineer team so large changes to shared files could ship safely with limited test environments.

Disruptions (Angular 15–20): adapted the disruption flow to run inside the BA mobile app, integrated the help team's new chatbot across teams, and built the frontend for a new stopover and connections feature, solving gaps in the backend data with frontend logic.

Ready to Travel (AWS IoT proof of concept): set up the Angular architecture as the team's most experienced Angular engineer, mocking data ahead of the backend, then moved onto AWS and Terraform backend work.
Ancillaries: helped deliver a brand-new cabin upgrade feature on legacy pages through to completion, including designing and building the page’s messaging component to match the newer design system.

experiences.title: Software engineer
description: Joined as a junior engineer and progressed to mid-level, working on a subscription-based Angular 9–12 platform for regulated businesses in the insurance sector.
Took over the International Regulators project from the Principal Engineer, building it out from his architecture through to delivery.
Helped build the in-app dashboards summarising tasks, notifications, document activity and network overviews, alongside the document exchange features.
Served as the team’s sole designer, producing UI designs in Adobe XD and Illustrator alongside my engineering work.
Contributed to frontend architecture decisions, improving component reusability across the platform.

projects.title: High Performance Gallery: Angular 21 + Node.js
projects.description: A deep-dive into performant image gallery design. This project showcases a bottom-up architectural transformation, rebuilding a sluggish 97.7 MB payload disaster into a lightning-fast experience with a 96+ Lighthouse score. Features database optimization with indexed queries, a custom Node.js/Sharp image processing pipeline, Angular Signals, and an optimized infinite scroll data delivery strategy for seamless asset loading.

projects.title: Component Lab: Accessible Headless UI
projects.description: A deep-dive into enterprise-grade component design. This project showcases the implementation of 'headless' UI patterns—separating complex accessibility logic from visual styling. Featuring WCAG-compliant components built with the new Angular Aria library, including focus-trapped modals and screen-reader-optimised comboboxes.

projects.title: Reactive MEAN Stack: Signal-Based Task Management
projects.description: An exploration of modern Angular reactivity, replacing traditional Change Detection with Signal-based state. This MEAN stack application demonstrates full CRUD capabilities alongside a dedicated Server-Status utility, showcasing cross-stack health checks and responsive data-fetching patterns.
